source_metadata.title: Comparison of safety and efficacy of lower-intensity versus standard unfractionated heparin infusion nomograms for extracranial venous thromboembolism in the neurological intensive care unit
source_metadata.institution: Washington University School of Medicine / Barnes-Jewish Hospital Neurology/Neurosurgery ICU

atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to compare the safety and efficacy of a lower-intensity UFH nomogram with standard-intensity UFH and with no therapeutic anticoagulation in neurocritical care patients with acute extracranial VTE at risk of intracranial hemorrhage.
The study was a single-center retrospective observational cohort study at Washington University School of Medicine/Barnes-Jewish Hospital using a prospective Neuro ICU database.

Treatment strategy was selected by treating clinical teams using individualized assessments of hemorrhagic risk, thromboembolic risk, intracranial imaging stability, timing from neurologic injury or neurosurgical intervention, and overall clinical status.
Eligible patients were at least 18 years old, were admitted to the Neurology/Neurosurgery ICU between June 2018 and April 2024, and were diagnosed with acute DVT and/or PE during hospitalization.

population.label: Eligible Neuro ICU patients
inclusion_criteria: Acute DVT and/or PE diagnosed during hospitalization
Neurology/Neurosurgery ICU admission between June 2018 and April 2024

atoms.canonical_statement: Exclusions included absence of intracranial/intraspinal pathology, cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, non-UFH therapeutic anticoagulation, UFH duration under 24 hours, failure to reach therapeutic aPTT goal, hospital stay under 48 hours, early death, pregnancy, or incarceration.

population.label: Study exclusion criteria
exclusion_criteria: Failure to reach therapeutic aPTT goal

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with isolated distal DVT were excluded from the efficacy analysis but remained eligible for the safety analysis if they received UFH infusion.
The standard-intensity UFH nomogram targeted an aPTT of 60–100 seconds.
The lower-intensity UFH nomogram targeted an aPTT of 40–65 seconds.

Patients in the no-therapeutic-anticoagulation group received intermittent pneumatic compression on admission and heparin chemoprophylaxis 24–48 hours after the initial brain injury, intervention, or surgery.

exposures.details: Intermittent pneumatic compression on admission and heparin chemoprophylaxis 24–48 hours after initial brain injury/intervention/surgery

atoms.canonical_statement: DVT and PE testing was performed based on clinical suspicion; PE was confirmed by CT pulmonary angiography and DVT by venous duplex ultrasonography.
Symptomatic extracranial VTE progression was a co-primary outcome and was defined as quantifiable imaging progression of thrombus burden or a new PE after a prior DVT diagnosis.

outcome.definition: Quantifiable increase in thrombus burden on imaging or development of a new pulmonary embolism after a prior DVT diagnosis

atoms.canonical_statement: Major bleeding was a co-primary outcome and was defined using ISTH major-bleeding criteria.

outcome.definition: ISTH major bleeding: critical-site bleeding, transfusion of at least 2 units pRBCs outside the operating room, hemorrhagic shock, or hemoglobin decrease of at least 2 g/dL attributable to hemorrhage

atoms.canonical_statement: Intracranial hemorrhagic worsening was operationalized using clinical and imaging criteria, including symptomatic neurologic worsening, subdural hematoma thickness increase greater than 5 mm, ECASS HI-2 or higher hemorrhagic transformation, quantifiable tumor-bed bleeding, or intracerebral hematoma growth of at least 6 mL and 33%.

outcome.definition: Clinical or radiographic worsening using pathology-specific thresholds described in the protocol

atoms.canonical_statement: Minor hemorrhage was defined as bleeding that did not meet ISTH major-bleeding criteria.

outcome.definition: Bleeding not meeting ISTH major hemorrhage criteria

atoms.canonical_statement: Confirmed heparin-induced thrombocytopenia required a positive heparin-PF4 antibody ELISA plus a positive heparin-induced platelet aggregation assay or serotonin release assay.

outcome.definition: Positive heparin-PF4 antibody ELISA plus positive functional assay

atoms.canonical_statement: Thromboembolic and hemorrhagic events occurring after hospital discharge were not captured.

Multivariable regression assessed associations between anticoagulation strategy and co-primary outcomes; covariates were selected a priori, and Firth penalized logistic regression was used for sensitivity analyses.

For UFH target-attainment analysis, each aPTT measurement was classified relative to the assigned nomogram as below, within, or above target, patient-level percentages were calculated, and group medians were compared using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test.

Of 10,883 Neuro ICU admissions, 443 patients were diagnosed with acute DVT or PE; 236 met criteria for the safety cohort, including 81 standard-intensity UFH, 50 lower-intensity UFH, and 105 no therapeutic anticoagulation.

population.label: Adult Neurology/Neurosurgery ICU patients with acute extracranial DVT and/or PE and intracranial or intraspinal pathology who met study criteria

atoms.canonical_statement: The efficacy cohort excluded two isolated distal-DVT patients from each UFH group, leaving 79 standard-intensity UFH, 48 lower-intensity UFH, and 105 no-therapeutic-anticoagulation patients.

population.label: Efficacy cohort after excluding isolated distal DVT from each UFH group

atoms.canonical_statement: Age, sex, racial composition, BMI, PESI class, GCS, and stroke-subset NIHSS were similar across treatment groups, while CNS diagnosis distribution differed; the lower-intensity UFH group contained more intracerebral-hemorrhage and postoperative neurosurgical patients.

population.label: Adult Neurology/Neurosurgery ICU patients with acute extracranial DVT and/or PE and intracranial or intraspinal pathology who met study criteria

atoms.canonical_statement: Major bleeding occurred in 15 of 81 standard-intensity UFH patients (18.5%) and 2 of 50 lower-intensity UFH patients (4.0%), with p=0.02.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that lower-intensity UFH was associated with fewer major bleeding events than standard-intensity UFH, without a significant difference in VTE progression between UFH strategies, and may offer a reasonable thrombotic–hemorrhagic balance in selected brain-injured patients.
The single-center design and relatively small sample size may limit generalizability and statistical power for smaller between-group differences.
Because anticoagulation strategy was selected by clinical judgment rather than random assignment, confounding by indication and residual confounding may remain despite adjusted analyses.

VTE diagnosis and follow-up imaging were based on clinical suspicion rather than standardized surveillance, creating potential ascertainment bias and possible under-detection of asymptomatic or subclinical VTE progression.

The cohort focused on extracranial VTE treated medically with UFH and excluded patients requiring initial thrombectomy, catheter-directed therapy, or other invasive interventions, limiting applicability across the full spectrum of VTE presentations.
The study reported no specific funding from public, commercial, or not-for-profit funding agencies.
The authors declared no conflicts of interest.

extraction_limitations: The extraction is limited to the main 8-page article PDF; supplementary tables/figures referenced by the article were not supplied as separate source files.

The narrative description of baseline CNS-diagnosis differences on page 3 and the p-values visible in Table 1 on page 4 are not perfectly concordant; the atom records the qualitative imbalance without normalizing the discrepant p-values.

The direction/reference category for the adjusted OR 0.85 comparing the two UFH strategies is not explicit in the surrounding sentence; the atom preserves the reported estimate without assigning a directional interpretation.

Clinical-suspicion-driven diagnostic and follow-up imaging means the study did not systematically ascertain asymptomatic VTE progression; this is preserved as a reported limitation rather than repaired by inference.
All atoms remain marked needs_review because no human source verification was performed after model extraction.
